transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Um... so, the main thing that pushed me to finally make an appointment and come in today is... well, it's about my job. I work as an insurance claims clerk, which is, you know, a lot of sitting. I have this workstation with two monitors, and I'm supposed to just sit there and go through policies all day. I only have some college, so getting this office job was actually a pretty big deal for me, and I really want to do well. 

But I just... I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Like, constantly. Even when I know, I mean I *really* know, that I’m supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews. We have these daily quotas, right? A certain number of claims we have to get through by the end of the shift. And I’ll tell myself, 'Okay, just sit here and do this next batch,' but then... I don't know, fifteen minutes later I'm up again. 

I'll go get a drink of water, or I'll walk to the printer even if I didn't print anything, or I'll just sort of wander toward the breakroom just to look out the window. It's like my body just decides it's time to stand up, and before I even really process it, I'm away from my desk. My supervisor has started walking past my cubicle and noticing that my chair is empty, and it's making me really anxious. I know exactly what I'm supposed to be doing, and I want to do it, but staying planted in that seat to actually finish my reviews feels almost impossible sometimes. So, yeah, that's what brought me here.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, even when you're not trying to get up from your desk?

Oh, absolutely. It's not just the getting up, which is bad enough, but even when I do manage to glue myself to the chair, I'm never just... still. Like, for example, when we have these mandatory training sessions or those really long quarterly team meetings. They usually hold them in this big conference room on our floor, and the chairs are those heavy, ergonomic ones, but I am just constantly shifting around in them anyway. 

I'll be sitting there, trying so hard to look perfectly focused and professional because, like I said, this job is important to me, but my leg will just be going a mile a minute under the table. Just bouncing, bouncing, bouncing. And if I manage to stop my leg because I suddenly realize the person next to me is getting annoyed by the table vibrating, then my hands just automatically take over. I'll grab a pen and start clicking it. I honestly don't even realize I'm doing it until someone gives me a look, and then I have to put the pen down, but then I'll just start taking the cap off and putting it back on, or peeling the label off my water bottle. 

I'm just always crossing my legs, uncrossing them, leaning forward, leaning back. It's like this buzzing feeling under my skin that just has to get out somehow. So even when I am technically sitting down and trying my absolute hardest to look like I'm paying attention to the PowerPoint or whatever the manager is talking about, I'm still just constantly in motion. It's exhausting, honestly, just trying to sit normally like everyone else seems to be able to do without even thinking about it.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of persistent restlessness, difficulty staying seated, and near-constant motor activity (e.g., leg bouncing, fidgeting, inability to remain still) are highly consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation. This presentation is most specific for F90.0.
